title: CohRing: Abstract Model of H*(BG; k) for Cyclic Groups
content: **CohRing** models the cohomology ring $H^*(BG; k)$ of the classifying space $BG$ for cyclic groups. The structure stores: `groupOrder` ($|G|$), `genDeg` (degree of the polynomial generator $u$), and `valid` ($|G| \geq 2$). The `cohRing` constructor sets `genDeg = 1` for $G = \mathbb{Z}/2$ and `genDeg = 2` for $G = \mathbb{Z}/p$ with $p$ odd. This matches the actual cohomology: $H^*(B\mathbb{Z}/2; \mathbb{F}_2) \cong \mathbb{F}_2[u]$ with $|u| = 1$, and $H^*(B\mathbb{Z}/p; \mathbb{F}_p) \cong \mathbb{F}_p[u] \otimes \Lambda[v]$ with $|u| = 2$ (for $p$ odd).
mathContext: The classifying space $B\mathbb{Z}/p$ is the infinite lens space $L^\infty(p) = S^\infty/(\mathbb{Z}/p)$. Its cohomology: $H^*(B\mathbb{Z}/2; \mathbb{F}_2) = \mathbb{F}_2[u]$ (polynomial on one generator of degree 1); $H^*(B\mathbb{Z}/p; \mathbb{F}_p) = \mathbb{F}_p[u] \otimes \Lambda(v)$ for odd $p$ (polynomial generator $u$ of degree 2, exterior generator $v$ of degree 1). The FH index uses only the polynomial part $\mathbb{F}_p[u]$, since index ideals are generated by even-degree classes. The `genDeg` field captures the degree of $u$, which determines how the FH index translates to dimension bounds: $\text{Index}_{\mathbb{Z}/p}(S^{2n-1}) = (u^n)$ has degree $n \cdot \text{genDeg}$.
relatedConcepts: classifying space BG for discrete groups
polynomial generator u and exterior generator v
prerequisites: Classifying spaces and their cohomology rings

title: FHIndex: The Fadell-Husseini Index as a Principal Ideal
content: **FHIndex** represents the Fadell-Husseini index $\text{Index}_G(X) \subseteq H^*(BG; k)$ as the minimum power $m$ with $u^m \in \text{Index}_G(X)$. For cyclic groups, the index ideal is always principal: $\text{Index}_G(X) = (u^m)$, so this single natural number captures all the information. Three constructors: **fullIndex** ($m = 0$, whole ring, equivariantly contractible space), **zeroIndex** ($m = \text{none}$, zero ideal, free action), **powerIndex** ($m = n$, the sphere computation $(u^n)$).
mathContext: The FH index $\text{Index}_G(X)$ is defined as $\ker(H^*(BG) \to H^*(X \times_G EG))$ — the kernel of the Borel construction map. For $G = \mathbb{Z}/p$ cyclic, $H^*(BG) = \mathbb{F}_p[u]$ is a PID, so every ideal is principal: $\text{Index}_G(X) = (u^m)$ for some $m \in \{0, 1, 2, \ldots\} \cup \{\infty\}$. The value $m = 0$ means the whole ring (i.e., $H^*(X \times_G EG) = 0$, possible when $X$ is contractible). The value $m = \infty$ (represented as `none`) means the kernel is 0 (free action, all of $H^*(BG)$ injects into $H^*(X_{hG})$). **Monotonicity of ideal index**: if $f: X \to Y$ is a $G$-equivariant map, then $\text{Index}_G(Y) \subseteq \text{Index}_G(X)$, i.e., $m_X \leq m_Y$ in terms of minimum powers.
prerequisites: Principal ideal domains and ideal containment

title: fh_sphere_free_action: Index(S^{2n-1}) = (u^n) — The Key Sphere Computation
content: **fh_sphere_free_action**: For a prime $p$ and $n \geq 1$, the FH index of $S^{2n-1}$ with the standard free $\mathbb{Z}/p$ action (rotation in $\mathbb{C}^n$) is $\text{Index}_{\mathbb{Z}/p}(S^{2n-1}) = (u^n)$, encoded as `minPower = some n`. The proof is `rfl` — it's definitional from `powerIndex`. This is the **central computation** that drives all the BU dimension theorems.
mathContext: The Borel construction $S^{2n-1} \times_{\mathbb{Z}/p} E\mathbb{Z}/p$ is the total space of a $\mathbb{Z}/p$-bundle over $B\mathbb{Z}/p = L^\infty(p)$ with fiber $S^{2n-1}$. This total space is the $(2n-1)$-dimensional lens space $L^{2n-1}(p) = S^{2n-1}/(\mathbb{Z}/p)$ (up to homotopy), and $H^*(L^{2n-1}(p); \mathbb{F}_p) \cong \mathbb{F}_p[u]/(u^n) \otimes \Lambda(v)$ (truncated polynomial). The Borel map $H^*(B\mathbb{Z}/p) \to H^*(L^{2n-1}(p))$ sends $u \mapsto u$ and has kernel $(u^n)$. Therefore $\text{Index}_{\mathbb{Z}/p}(S^{2n-1}) = (u^n)$. That the proof is `rfl` shows this deep topological fact is **encoded into the axioms** via `powerIndex` — the computation is captured at the axiom level, not proved here.
relatedConcepts: free Z/p action on S^{2n-1} via rotation in C^n
prerequisites: Lens spaces as quotients of spheres by free cyclic actions

title: fh_implies_buDim_lower_bound: FH Index → BU Dimension Lower Bound
content: **fh_implies_buDim_lower_bound**: For prime $p$ and $n \geq 1$, $2n-1 \leq \text{buDim}(p, 2n)$. The proof: `buDim_prime p n hp hn` from the parent file gives $\text{buDim}(p, 2n) = 2n-1$ exactly, so `omega` closes $2n-1 \leq 2n-1$. This is the **FH index → dimension lower bound** principle: since $\text{Index}_{\mathbb{Z}/p}(S^{2n-1}) = (u^n)$ and the FH index satisfies $\text{Index}_{\mathbb{Z}/p}(S^m) \supseteq (u^n)$ iff $m \geq 2n-1$, we need at least $m = 2n-1$ for an equivariant map to exist.
mathContext: The general FH lower bound argument: $\text{buDim}(G, d) \geq m$ iff $\text{Index}_G(S^{m-1}) \supsetneq \text{Index}_G(S(V_d))$ (where $V_d$ is the $d$-dimensional representation). For $G = \mathbb{Z}/p$, $d = 2n$, $S(V_{2n}) = S^{2n-1}$ with $\text{Index} = (u^n)$, and $\text{Index}_{\mathbb{Z}/p}(S^m) = (u^{\lfloor(m+1)/2\rfloor})$. So we need $(u^n) \supseteq (u^{\lfloor(m+1)/2\rfloor})$, i.e., $\lfloor(m+1)/2\rfloor \leq n$, i.e., $m \leq 2n-1$. Combined with the matching upper bound from an explicit construction, $\text{buDim}(p, 2n) = 2n-1$ (the Yang-Borsuk theorem).
relatedConcepts: Yang-Borsuk theorem for prime cyclic groups
FH index lower bound via containment of principal ideals

title: fh_recovers_yang_borsuk: The FH Framework Recovers the Yang-Borsuk Theorem
content: **fh_recovers_yang_borsuk**: $\text{buDim}(p, 2n) = 2n-1$ for prime $p$. One-line alias of `buDim_prime` from the parent file. This theorem demonstrates **consistency**: the FH index computation (Index$(S^{2n-1}) = (u^n)$) is consistent with the axiomatized buDim values. The FH framework is not adding new information here — it is showing its framework agrees with the pre-existing Yang-Borsuk axiom.
mathContext: The **Yang-Borsuk theorem** (C.T. Yang, 1954; K. Borsuk, 1967): for a prime $p$ and the standard free $\mathbb{Z}/p$ action on $S^{2n-1}$, the equivariant BU dimension is $\text{buDim}(\mathbb{Z}/p, 2n) = 2n-1$. This is proved topologically using Smith theory: any equivariant map $S^{2n-1} \to S^m$ requires $m \geq 2n-1$ (lower bound from fixed point theory), and the identity map gives $m = 2n-1$ (upper bound from explicit construction). The FH index formulation gives an algebraic proof of the lower bound via $\text{Index}(S^{2n-1}) \not\subseteq \text{Index}(S^{2n-2})$.
relatedConcepts: equivariant BU dimension for prime groups
prerequisites: Smith theory for periodic fixed point estimates

title: fh_z4_bound: BU Dimension for Z/4 via Z/2 Restriction
content: **fh_z4_bound**: $2n-1 \leq \text{buDim}(4, 2n)$ for $n \geq 1$. The proof: `buDim_mono 2 4` (monotonicity since $2|4$) gives $\text{buDim}(2, 2n) \leq \text{buDim}(4, 2n)$, and `buDim_prime 2 n` gives $2n-1 = \text{buDim}(2, 2n)$, so omega closes $2n-1 \leq \text{buDim}(4, 2n)$. This is the **FH restriction map** argument: the inclusion $\mathbb{Z}/2 \hookrightarrow \mathbb{Z}/4$ induces a restriction map on cohomology, and the FH index of a $\mathbb{Z}/4$-space restricts to the FH index of the underlying $\mathbb{Z}/2$-space.
mathContext: For $G = \mathbb{Z}/4$, the restriction map $\text{res}: H^*(B\mathbb{Z}/4; \mathbb{F}_2) \to H^*(B\mathbb{Z}/2; \mathbb{F}_2)$ sends the generator $u_4$ (degree 2) to $u_2^2$ (degree 2). So $\text{Index}_{\mathbb{Z}/4}(S^{2n-1}) \ni u_4^n$, and restriction gives $u_2^{2n} \in \text{Index}_{\mathbb{Z}/2}(S^{2n-1})$. The $\mathbb{Z}/2$ index is $(u_2^n)$ (lower power), so $u_2^{2n} = (u_2^n)^2$ is in the index — this is weaker information. The **open question** (meta.json): does the $\mathbb{Z}/4$ FH index give the same bound as $\mathbb{Z}/2$, or is $\text{buDim}(4, 2n) > 2n-1$? Current evidence: they match for small $n$.
relatedConcepts: composite group FH index via subgroup restriction

title: fh_z6_bound: BU Dimension for Z/6 via Two Restriction Maps
content: **fh_z6_bound**: $2n-1 \leq \text{buDim}(6, 2n)$. Uses `z6_lower_bound_z3` from the parent file (via the $\mathbb{Z}/3 \subset \mathbb{Z}/6$ restriction). The FH framework gives two independent constraints for $G = \mathbb{Z}/6 = \mathbb{Z}/2 \times \mathbb{Z}/3$: restriction to $\mathbb{Z}/2$ gives $2n-1 \leq \text{buDim}(2, 2n) \leq \text{buDim}(6, 2n)$, and restriction to $\mathbb{Z}/3$ gives the same bound. Both give the same lower bound $2n-1$, suggesting $\text{buDim}(6, 2n) = 2n-1$.
mathContext: For $G = \mathbb{Z}/6$, the two prime subgroups $\mathbb{Z}/2 \subset \mathbb{Z}/6$ and $\mathbb{Z}/3 \subset \mathbb{Z}/6$ each give restriction maps. The **conjectured formula** (buDim for composite groups): $\text{buDim}(n, d) = \max_{p|n, p \text{ prime}} \text{buDim}(p, d)$. For $n=6$: $\max(\text{buDim}(2, 2n), \text{buDim}(3, 2n)) = \max(2n-1, 2n-1) = 2n-1$. If this conjecture is true, $\text{buDim}(6, 2n) = 2n-1$ exactly. The FH restriction map argument gives the lower bound; the upper bound would require an explicit equivariant map construction.
relatedConcepts: Z/6 = Z/2 × Z/3 direct product decomposition
two restriction maps for composite groups
Chinese Remainder Theorem for cyclic groups

title: fh_extends_monotonicity: The FH Framework Subsumes Monotonicity
content: **fh_extends_monotonicity** states that the FH framework contains monotonicity as a special case: $\forall p, n, d : p \mid n \Rightarrow \text{buDim}(p, d) \leq \text{buDim}(n, d)$. The proof is a one-liner calling `buDim_mono`. This is a **meta-theorem**: it shows the FH framework subsumes the simpler monotonicity approach from the parent file, serving as a sanity check on the formalization. The FH framework additionally gives two-sided bounds and product formulas that monotonicity alone cannot provide.
mathContext: Monotonicity of buDim ($p|n \Rightarrow \text{buDim}(p,d) \leq \text{buDim}(n,d)$) is the algebraic consequence of the restriction map $H^*(BG) \to H^*(BH)$ for $H \leq G$: restricting a $G$-action to $H$ gives an $H$-equivariant map, and the FH index can only decrease (ideal containment $\subseteq$) under this restriction. Algebraically: $\text{Index}_G(X) \supseteq \text{res}^* \text{Index}_H(X)$, so $m_G \leq m_H$ in terms of minimum powers. The theorem here confirms that `buDim_mono` (axiomatized in the parent) is consistent with this FH-derived monotonicity. The FH framework adds: product formula $\text{Index}(X \times Y) \supseteq \text{Index}(X) \cdot \text{Index}(Y)$, which is the algebraic content beyond simple monotonicity.
relatedConcepts: FH index monotonicity under group restriction
